key_insight: A wave-particle decomposition splits multiscale kinetic transport into a macroscopic wave and a residual particle part, yielding a continuous bridge from kinetic theory to Navier-Stokes that adapts locally by flow regime.
engineering_relevance: The framework provides an asymptotic-preserving solver strategy for steady multiscale flows, enabling faster convergence and efficient simulation of hypersonic and other near-continuum-to-kinetic regimes.
method: Define the wave as the local equilibrium integral along characteristics over a kinetic horizon, with the particle as its exact complement.
Evolve coupled equations: a macroscopic iteration for conservative variables and a kinetic iteration for the particle.
Use the horizon-to-relaxation ratio to tune the decomposition and recover a spectrum from kinetic to hydrodynamic behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hypersonic-cylinder and 3D X38 vehicle computations showing adaptive wave/particle partitioning and strong acceleration of the fixed-point iteration.
watch_item: Performance and accuracy depend on choosing the horizon relative to relaxation time, and the coupled iteration is described for steady flows rather than fully general unsteady settings.
paper_title: A wave-particle decomposition framework for multiscale kinetic transport: continuous-spectrum equations and coupled wave-particle iteration
